structure.note: Roche has 106,691,000 bearer shares, which carry the votes, and 702,562,700 non-voting equity securities (Genussscheine), which are not part of the share capital and confer no voting rights but share equally in profits and liquidation proceeds. A shareholder group with pooled voting rights (members of the Hoffmann and Oeri founding families, the charitable foundation Wolf and Artuma Holding LLC; pooling agreement in place since 1948) owned 69,318,000 shares, or 64.97% of the issued (voting) shares, at 31 December 2024. Maja Oeri, formerly in the pool, held 8,091,900 shares (7.58% of issued shares) independently. Both percentages are of the bearer shares only, not of all equity securities, so neither is listed as an economic holder here.

notes: All figures from Roche's own Annual Report 2024 and Finance Report 2024 PDFs on assets.roche.com (linked from roche.com/investors/annualreport24), fiscal year ended 31 December 2024, CHF converted exactly from CHF millions. OWNERSHIP: Severin Schwan (Chairman; his equity awards are listed as 'awarded in former role as CEO', hence relation 'chair') held 254,090 bearer shares and 102,071 non-voting equity securities (NES) at 31 December 2024; no percentage is given, so pctEconomic is null (for reference only, 356,161 of 809,253,700 equity securities is about 0.04%; not disclosed). shares records the bearer shares only. FOUNDING-FAMILY POOL (pctBasis): the 64.97% held by the shareholder group with pooled voting rights is a percentage of the 106,691,000 issued bearer shares, i.e. a share of the votes, not of all equity. The Genussscheine (702,562,700) carry the same economic rights as shares but no votes, so the pool's economic share of all equity securities is far lower; the report does not state it, so it is not derived or recorded. The pool is not Schwan's holding (he is not a member), so it is not placed in leader.family; it is described in structure.note. Maja Oeri's 7.58% is on the same bearer-share basis. The 'controlled: true' flag rests on the pool's 64.97% of voting shares. No other holders are disclosed, so largestHolders is empty. The company keeps no share register (bearer shares); holdings are 'based on the information available to the Group'. DIVIDENDS: CHF 7,650m to Roche shareholders; the cash-flow total of CHF (8,043)m also includes CHF 301m to Chugai minorities, CHF 59m to other minorities and CHF 33m withholding tax, excluded. BUYBACKS: 0 under the site's rule that purchases covering employee plans are not cash returned to shareholders (same rule as the Tencent pilot and the UBS and Fortescue records). Roche ran no buyback programme in 2024 and Roche Holding Ltd itself 'neither purchased nor sold' shares or NES. Group companies had a net cash outflow of CHF 1,093m from 'Transactions in own equity' (Note 27), which the report says mainly relates to equity instruments held for equity compensation plan obligations; it sits in the cash-flow line 'Equity-settled equity compensation plans, net of transactions in own equity (1,130)'. To count it instead, use 1.09 (net). STOCK COMP: CHF 855m equity compensation plan expense (all equity-settled). GEOGRAPHY: the Sales column only (CHF 60,495m), which excludes CHF 1,900m of other revenue (royalties etc.).

footprint.notes: Roche publishes employees by region only (Annual Report 2024 chart; FTEs at Dec 31, 2024, total 103,249). The regions are Roche's own groupings with no country list, except Australia/New Zealand. No country or U.S. state breakdown of employees, sites or taxes was found in the Annual Report or the Finance Report 2024 (the Finance Report gives only group income taxes paid, CHF 3,727 million). Roche does not file with the SEC. The Annual Report PDF is served from Roche's asset CDN (assets.roche.com), linked from roche.com/investors/annualreport24. Sites are those the report itself names; Roche does not list its major facilities in the Annual Report. State codes for the U.S. sites come from the place names (the report says only "(US)"). Genentech's Investing in America page (gene.com) gives national post-2025 commitment figures ($50B, 28 facilities), not per-state values for FY2024, so it was not used.
